answers.text:
In this modern life many service like the bank, the bill and the appointment of the doctor is only in the internet or in the application. Some people think this is a good thing and other people think it is a bad thing. I want to write the advantage and the disadvantage of this situation.

Firstly, the advantage is very clear. The people don't go to the office and don't wait in a long queue for one hour. They open the phone in the house and in five minute the work is finish. Also the internet don't close in the night, so a person who work all the day can pay the bill at eleven o'clock in the night. This save the time and also the money of the transport.

Secondly, there is many disadvantage too. The old people don't know how to use the application and they are afraid to make a mistake with the money. Also some people in the village don't have a good connection and they cannot enter to the system. When the application have a problem, there is nobody for help you and you must call a telephone number and wait very long time.

In my country my grandmother cannot pay her bill alone and every month my father must do it for her. This is not a good situation for a old person.

In conclusion, the online service have a big advantage and also a big disadvantage. Both of them are important and every person must decide alone which one is more strong for him.

why_this_band.task_response: Both sides are covered, but no judgement is given at the end: saying 'both of them are important' leaves the weighing question unanswered, when the task asks for a decision on which side is stronger. The grandmother example stays on topic but does no more than repeat a single disadvantage.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: There is a Firstly / Secondly / In conclusion sequence, and advantages and disadvantages are in separate paragraphs, so it can be followed. The fourth paragraph starts without linking to the previous one, and the progression breaks down there.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The phrases good thing, bad thing, save the time, big advantage are repeated; there is no item specific to online services. Enter to the system and the work is finish are wrong in form.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Agreement and article errors are common: the internet don't close, there is many disadvantage, the application have, a old person, the online service have. The structures amount to no more than simple sentences joined with and/also.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Replace the final paragraph's 'both are important' with a clear judgement: which side outweighs the other, and why. This is exactly what the task asks for.

answers.text:
A growing number of everyday services, from banking to booking a medical appointment, can now only be reached through a website or an application. In my view the benefits of this change are greater than the drawbacks, but only if some alternative is kept for those who cannot use a screen.

The main advantage is convenience. A transaction that used to require a bus journey, a queue and half a morning off work can now be completed in a few minutes at any hour of the day or night. This is particularly valuable for people with long working hours or small children, who find very difficult to visit an office between nine and five. Organisations also spend less on buildings and counter staff, and a part of this saving usually return to the customer in the form of lower charges.

However, the disadvantages should not be minimised. Elderly people who has never used a computer, and households in areas with a weak connection, can suddenly find themselves unable to do something they have always done. When the system breaks down, moreover, there is nobody in front of you to explain the problem, and a telephone helpline with a waiting time of forty minutes is a poor replacement for a member of staff.

Overall, I think the advantages do outweigh the disadvantages, because they are felt by the great majority every single week, while the serious difficulties falls on a smaller group. That group is real, however, so companies and public offices should be obliged to keep at least one non-digital way for doing the same thing.

why_this_band.task_response: The judgement is given in the introduction along with its condition (advantages outweigh, but only if an alternative channel remains), and repeated with the same condition at the end. The advantages are explained by stating who they apply to; the disadvantages section is accurate but stays limited to two groups.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The paragraph order is clear: judgement, advantages, disadvantages, weighing. The However and Overall transitions are correct but formulaic; within paragraphs the linking does not go beyond moreover.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Appropriate items such as convenience, transaction, helpline, charges, non-digital are present. Should not be minimised and a poor replacement for a member of staff are apt; find themselves unable is repeated somewhat.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, conditional structures and contrast connectors are correctly built; most sentences are error-free. Close to a third of sentences contain an error (who find very difficult to visit, who has never used, a part of this saving usually return, the serious difficulties falls, one non-digital way for doing); they do not stop the reader.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Build the weighing on a criterion rather than a headcount: in which situation the advantage outweighs, and in which it does not. The decision is currently correct, but its reasoning is confined to one sentence.

answers.text:
Banking, paying bills and arranging appointments have quietly migrated to the screen, and in many cases the older counter or telephone route has been closed altogether. Weighed against each other, the gains are substantial enough to justify the shift, though only where a non-digital route survives alongside it.

What has been gained is chiefly time. A task that once meant an hour of queuing, and often an hour taken from the working day, is now finished in a few minutes at whatever hour suits the user. For anyone juggling shift work or childcare, that difference is not a minor convenience but the difference between managing their affairs and postponing them indefinitely. There is a second, less visible gain: a digital record leaves the customer with proof of what was agreed, which used to depend on whoever happened to be behind the desk.

Against this stands a genuine risk of exclusion. A person of eighty who has never owned a computer, or a household on a patchy rural connection, does not simply find the new arrangement less convenient; they find the service unreachable. Failures are harder to resolve as well, since an automated system that rejects an application cannot be reasoned with, and a helpline queue is a poor substitute for someone who can look at the file with you.

My judgement is that the advantages prevail, because they are enjoyed constantly by most users while the losses, though severe, are concentrated on a minority. That conclusion carries a condition, however: it holds only for as long as providers are required to keep one staffed alternative open. Remove that, and the balance tips the other way for the people least able to complain about it.

why_this_band.task_response: The judgement is clear and conditional: advantages outweigh, but only for as long as a staffed alternative remains open. Both sides are broken down by what they mean for whom, and the conclusion states that removing the condition tips the balance the other way.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The text moves through gains, losses and judgement; each paragraph carries a single claim. Transitions such as Against this stands and That conclusion carries a condition connect by carrying forward the previous paragraph's conclusion.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items such as migrated to the screen, patchy rural connection, concentrated on a minority, staffed alternative are accurate and natural. The choice of cannot be reasoned with sums up the problem with automated systems in a single phrase.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Inverted structure (Against this stands...), a semicolon-linked contrast and nested relative clauses are handled with control. Errors are rare; the short sentence in the final paragraph is deliberately used for emphasis.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tie the second advantage, the record that is kept, to a consequence as well; it is currently accurate but less developed than the other points.
